data.content:

November 9, 2026

This is some text inside of a div block.

This is some text inside of a div block.

While every bank relies on so-called “stop lists” to preserve fraud memory, the critical absence of regulatory standardization turns these essential tools into operational liabilities that either miss repeat threats or block legitimate growth.

## Listen to this article

## Key insights: [...] September’s federal actions make that question unusually concrete. The novelty is not another pandemic-fraud scheme, because those have been known for years. What is more significant is the response because SBA’s September action combined suspension from future programs with repayment demands, collection by the U.S. Treasury Department, and potential law-enforcement referral. In other words, identified risk no longer matters only to yesterday’s investigation — it can shape tomorrow’s [...] ## The danger of going too far

For banks, that is where the analogy becomes useful and dangerous if taken too far. A federal suspension, fraud finding, or adverse program decision may be highly relevant, but that relevance does not automatically mean equivalence. Banks still need to determine how that signal actually maps to their own legal obligations, risk appetite, and customer relationships.
